Configuration: arguments and thresholds

2026-11-09

Source: vignettes/configuration.Rmd
configuration.Rmd

Authoritative index of every user-configurable component of the algorithm. For reference, hard-coded numeric threshold and reference-data-driven values are also provided. The algorithm vignettes (vignette("child-algorithm"), vignette("wrapper"), vignette("adult-algorithm")) cite this reference for defaults and thresholds rather than duplicating them.

If you are interested in the adult permissiveness presets, see Section 1D.

How to Read This Reference

Three categories:

  1. Arguments — arguments to cleangrowth() that change how growthcleanr cleans, runs, or what it returns. Organized by algorithm scope.
  2. Hardcoded thresholds — numeric values baked into the code; a caller cannot change them without downloading and editing the package code. These are provided for reference and are organized by step.
  3. Reference-data-driven values — loaded from external files in inst/extdata/ or defined in large lookup tables. Some can be replaced with your own values: sd.recenter takes a table of recentering medians (or "none" to turn recentering off), and ref.data.path points to a folder of reference files. Non-configurable, hard-coded reference-data-driven values are provided for reference.

Sections per category:

  • Argument/threshold name (as written in code)
  • Value (default for configurable; literal for hardcoded; “see file X” for ref-data)
  • Scope (step, phase, or algorithm)
  • Code location (file + function + sub-section)
  • Brief role

Conventions:

  • < / > = strict inequalities unless noted
  • Param values: "WEIGHTKG", "HEIGHTCM", "HEADCM" (after input conversion)
  • Sex: 0 = male, 1 = female
  • All adult threshold comparisons include the 0.12 cm/kg adult rounding tolerance unless explicitly noted otherwise
  • Exclusion-code strings shown in this reference are the algorithm’s internal literals (e.g. Exclude-C-PIV, Exclude-Missing, Exclude-Not-Cleaned, Exclude-A-Scale-Max) — the values the code assigns and tests internally. growthcleanr maps these to the user-facing Summary (exclude) and Detailed (exclude_detailed) output codes at output assembly; the internal literals are unchanged. For the output codes and the internal→Summary/Detailed crosswalk, see vignette("exclusion-codes").

1. User arguments

1A. Wrapper-level (exposed in cleangrowth() signature)

Ready-to-run scripts for the most common of these (column names, sex_coding, param_coding, dates, input_format, parallel and checkpointing, adult settings) are in vignette("example-scripts").

Argument Default Used in Role
id NULL (optional) cleangrowth preprocessing; output Unique row identifier. Fully optional. When absent / NULL / contains NA / not unique, a warning is issued and sequential ids 1:N (in input row order) are auto-generated for internal use. The user’s original id (whatever was supplied — even if invalid) is preserved untouched in the output id column. To see the id growthcleanr actually used internally (= user’s id when valid, = regen otherwise), set display_gc_id = TRUE or full_detail = TRUE. Semi-wide/wide input: the id argument, or a column named id, identifies an input row (it need not be unique); growthcleanr mints its own per-measurement ids. In semi-wide input the id orders a subject’s visit rows when the minted ids are assigned (so it can decide which same-day value is kept when the id tiebreak applies); in wide input it does not affect cleaning. It is returned unchanged in semi-wide/wide output and, in long output, under its own column name on each measurement from that row, with growthcleanr’s number in gc_internal_id.
subjid (required) — column name in data (data-frame style) or a vector (vector style) cleangrowth preprocessing Subject identifier vector
param (required) — column name in data (data-frame style) or a vector (vector style) cleangrowth preprocessing Measurement-type vector. Canonical: WEIGHTKG, HEIGHTCM, LENGTHCM, HEADCM, WEIGHTLBS, HEIGHTIN, LENGTHIN, HEADIN. Matched case-insensitively. No built-in abbreviations — a bare WT/HT/HC is not assumed to be a gc parameter (may be a sample weight, etc.); map non-canonical labels with param_coding. See vignette("wrapper") → Flexible sex and parameter coding.
agedays (required) — column name in data (data-frame style) or a vector (vector style) cleangrowth preprocessing Age in days at measurement
sex (required) — column name in data (data-frame style) or a vector (vector style) cleangrowth preprocessing Sex indicator; default codes 0/"m"/"b"/"male"/"boy" = male, 1/"f"/"g"/"female"/"girl" = female (case-insensitive). Override with sex_coding. A 1=male/2=female column hard-stops unless declared. See vignette("wrapper") → Flexible sex and parameter coding.
sex_coding list(male = c(0, "m", "b", "male", "boy"), female = c(1, "f", "g", "female", "girl")) cleangrowth preprocessing (.gc_recode_sex, reshape_adapters.R) Named list (male, female) of the codes denoting each sex; case-insensitive, whitespace-trimmed. Supplying a table replaces the defaults wholesale and suppresses the 1/2 guard. Errors if a code is under both sexes. Present-but-unrecognized codes → Exclude-Missing-Info + warning.
param_coding NULL cleangrowth preprocessing (.gc_recode_param, reshape_adapters.R) Optional named list keyed by canonical parameter, values = your labels to remap (case-insensitive). The only way to have a non-canonical label recognized (there are no built-in abbreviations); also how you declare a remapped column is imperial (map to WEIGHTLBS/HEIGHTIN/LENGTHIN/HEADIN), else it defaults to its metric target. Errors if a name is not canonical or a label maps to two parameters.
measurement (required) — column name in data (data-frame style) or a vector (vector style) cleangrowth preprocessing Recorded value in units specified by param
input_format "long" cleangrowth input dispatch (Hook A, reshape_adapters.R) Shape of data: "long" (one row per measurement), "semi_wide" (one row per visit, one column per parameter), or "wide" (one row per subject, repeated observation blocks marked by a _N column suffix). Non-long input is reshaped to long before cleaning, so results match the equivalent long submission. Requires data-frame style. See vignette("wrapper") → Input format.
output_format NULL cleangrowth output (Hook B, reshape_adapters.R) Shape of the returned results: "long", "semi_wide", or "wide". NULL mirrors input_format, so semi-wide input returns semi-wide output and wide input returns wide output. Re-widened output returns the submitted table with the growthcleanr columns named in widened_emit slotted in beside each value column (exclude_wt_cm for semi-wide, exclude_wt_1 for wide); it requires the matching input format (checkpointed runs are supported). See Output format: semi-wide / wide in vignette("wrapper").
widened_emit "exclude" .gc_semiwide_output / .gc_wide_output (reshape_adapters.R) Which growthcleanr output columns to add to re-widened (semi-wide or wide) output. Any per-measurement column may be named ("bin_exclude", "exclude_detailed", "unit_error_range", "measurement", "agedays", …); naming one whose own switch is off is an error. gc output columns take the value-column suffix only (exclude_wt_kg; exclude_wt_1 for wide); gc’s internal version of a submitted value takes a gc_internal_ prefix (gc_internal_meas_wt_lbs). "measurement" also emits gc_internal_param_*. agedays is per visit in semi-wide, per block in wide (gc_internal_agedays_1, …). Used when output_format is "semi_wide" or "wide".
internal_detail FALSE Output assembly Adds gc_internal_meas, gc_internal_param, gc_internal_sex, gc_internal_id, and gc_internal_agedays – growthcleanr’s working values for the key inputs the user supplied (imperial converted to metric, LENGTHCM relabeled, sex coerced to 0/1, age as whole days; the length.adjust offset is applied only to z-scores, so it is not reflected in gc_internal_meas) – plus gc_internal_dob / gc_internal_visit_date when a dob / visit_date column was supplied. The primary columns always return the verbatim submission. The imperial conversion and the LENGTHCM relabel are reflected for every row. Enabled by full_detail.
semiwide_cols NULL .gc_semiwide_to_long (reshape_adapters.R) Named list/vector mapping gc parameters to their value columns for semi-wide input, e.g. list(WEIGHTKG = "wt_kg", HEIGHTCM = "ht_cm", HEADCM = "head_cm"). NULL uses columns literally named as recognized parameters. Only used when input_format = "semi_wide".
wide_cols NULL .gc_wide_to_long (reshape_adapters.R) Named list/vector mapping gc parameters to their column-name prefixes for wide input, e.g. list(WEIGHTKG = "wt", HEIGHTCM = "ht", HEADCM = "hc") for wt_1, wt_2, ht_1, …. The user picks the prefix; growthcleanr requires the _N block suffix and discovers blocks from it. NULL uses prefixes literally named as recognized parameters (WEIGHTKG_1, …). A mapped prefix with no <prefix>_N columns is an error. subjid/sex are patient-level; the age source is per block (agedays_N, or dob + visit_date_N). Only used when input_format = "wide".
max_blocks 25 .gc_wide_to_long (reshape_adapters.R) Highest number of wide observation blocks expected. Finding more warns (with guidance to raise it or reshape to long/semi-wide) but processes every block; an implausible count errors, since it usually means the _N suffixes parsed wrong. Only used when input_format = "wide".
dob NULL cleangrowth preprocessing (age) Date-of-birth column name (data-frame style only). Column is class Date or a text date; a subject with more than one distinct dob value is set aside as Exclude-Missing-Info, with a warning. Supplied with visit_date to compute agedays as floor(visit_date - dob) in whole days. Text dates parse under order-free formats — year-first numeric (2013-03-04, 2013/03/04, 20130304) or English spelled-month (03mar2013, March 15, 2024) — or, for numeric day/month (3/4/2013), only with date_order. All dates in dob/visit_date share one format; four-digit years 1900–2099 only. Blank/NA and text with no digits (e.g. N/A) -> missing agedays; a few dates that are not real dates are set aside, more than a few stop the run; numeric date integers are rejected. See vignette("wrapper") → Date parsing.
visit_date NULL cleangrowth preprocessing (age) Visit (measurement) date column name (data-frame style only). Class Date or a text date in the same accepted formats as dob. Supplied together with dob.
age_source NULL cleangrowth preprocessing (age) Which age source to resolve agedays from: "agedays" (the agedays column) or "dates" (dob + visit_date). NULL auto-resolves (an agedays column wins when present; otherwise the dates). Set "dates" to force date-based ages even when an agedays column is present. With "dates" and an age column present, that column is returned as submitted and the computed ages as gc_internal_agedays.
date_order NULL cleangrowth preprocessing (age) Day-vs-month order for ambiguous numeric dob/visit_date values (data-frame style only), e.g. "3/4/2013": "dmy" (day-month-year) or "mdy" (month-day-year), applied uniformly. NULL accepts only the order-free formats and errors on numeric day/month dates, so an ambiguous order is never guessed. growthcleanr never auto-detects order.
carry_through TRUE cleangrowth preprocessing; output Data-frame style only. When TRUE (default), columns in data that are not resolved role columns (subjid/param/agedays/sex/measurement/id) are parked and returned appended after the gc output columns (original order/values; dob/visit_date are echoed back this way). A carried column whose name matches a column gc returns in this run (e.g. exclude) is returned as userinput_<name>, with a warning; names of gc columns not returned in the run are left alone. FALSE drops all non-role columns (prior behavior). Semi-wide/wide input: with semi-wide/wide output your table is the output base (TRUE keeps every column, FALSE keeps the role, id and value columns); with long output, your other columns (including dob/visit_date; in wide, not the per-block columns) are repeated on each measurement from their row.
adult_cutpoint 20 Preprocessing (pediatric/adult split) Age (years) dividing pediatric/adult processing. Clamped to [18, 20], with a warning when a value is moved. growthcleanr never changes it based on the data (each subject is cleaned independently of the rest of the dataset); if it is left at the default and every known-age measurement is >= 18y with some in the 18-20y range, a warning suggests adult_cutpoint = 18 to clean those with the adult algorithm instead of the child path.
sd.recenter NA Recentering (Phase 11) Recentering medians: NA (built-in rcfile-resmoothed.csv.gz), "none" (no recentering; tbc.sd = sd.orig), or your own table (a data.table or data.frame with columns param, sex, agedays, rcmedian.sd), which must cover every param, sex, and agedays of the child measurements to be cleaned, or cleangrowth() stops. See vignette("recentering").
ref.data.path "" Preprocessing; Child Step 17 Override directory for reference files. "" uses package inst/extdata/.
batch_size 5000 Outer-wrapper batching Subjects per processing batch (the in-memory unit); must be a single positive whole number. Independent of checkpoint_size.
checkpoint TRUE Checkpointed runs (cleangrowth_checkpoint.R) Master on/off switch. TRUE (default) checkpoints to an ephemeral per-session temp dir, engaging only when subjects > checkpoint_size (small/typical data runs in memory, writing nothing); those files are auto-deleted (keep_checkpoints forced FALSE). FALSE disables checkpointing entirely (nothing written to disk) and overrides checkpoint_dir with a warning. Supplying checkpoint_dir makes checkpointing persistent + resumable. See vignette("large-datasets") for use; vignette("wrapper") -> Checkpointed runs for internals.
checkpoint_dir NULL Checkpointed runs (cleangrowth_checkpoint.R) Persistent, resumable checkpoint location. When set, split subjects into checkpoints of checkpoint_size, clean each checkpoint, persist it to a checkpoint_NNNN.rds file here, and combine at the end. NULL (default) uses the ephemeral temp dir described under checkpoint (or no checkpointing when checkpoint = FALSE). Result is identical to a single-pass run (incl. wide/semi-wide input/output).
checkpoint_size 5000 Checkpointed runs Subjects per checkpoint (the persist unit; one .rds per checkpoint), and the threshold above which the checkpoint = TRUE default engages. Independent of batch_size (batch_size < checkpoint_size allowed). Capped at 9999 checkpoints: a size that would exceed the cap is increased (with a warning if you set it).
checkpoint_resume FALSE Checkpointed runs Only meaningful with a persistent checkpoint_dir (forced FALSE on the ephemeral default). FALSE starts fresh (deletes prior checkpoint files); TRUE reuses existing checkpoint files (skips completed checkpoints) to resume an interrupted run.
keep_checkpoints TRUE Checkpointed runs TRUE leaves the per-checkpoint files after a successful run; FALSE deletes them once combined. Independent of checkpoint_resume. Forced FALSE on the ephemeral checkpoint = TRUE default (temp files are always cleaned up); the TRUE default applies when you set checkpoint_dir.
log_file NULL Checkpointed runs Only used when checkpoint_dir is set. Path to also append progress messages to (console always gets them unless quietly), so a colleague can monitor a long run remotely.
parallel FALSE Inner batching Run batches in parallel (foreach %dopar% dispatch)
cores NULL Inner batching Number of parallel workers when parallel = TRUE; NULL auto-detects min(8, detectCores() - 1), capped at 8. An explicit value above detectCores() is reduced to it. Ignored when parallel = FALSE
log.path NA Parallel logging Deprecated (warns when supplied); use log_file. Log directory for parallel mode
ref_tables NULL All reads Pre-loaded reference closures from gc_preload_refs(); skips per-call disk reads (~0.93 sec/call)
tri_exclude FALSE Output assembly Include tri_exclude column in output ("Include" / "Same-Day" / "Exclude")
corr_detail FALSE Output assembly Add corr_val (per-value: "Corrected" / "Uncorrected" / "Adult") and corr_pt (per-subject) correction-status columns
recenter_detail FALSE Output assembly Include the recentered CSD z-score columns tbc.sd, ctbc.sd, and rcmedian.sd (the per-row recentering median subtracted). Specialized output for a related tool in development. Child rows only (NA on adult).
qm_detail FALSE cleanchild per-step capture; output For a related package in development — not used in cleaning (see vignette("output") §5c). Emit ten per-step eligibility flags for the child cleaning steps (qm_elig_c_cf, qm_elig_c_hardlimit, qm_elig_c_eviltwins, qm_elig_c_trajextreme, qm_elig_extraneous, qm_elig_c_traj, qm_elig_c_absdiff, qm_elig_c_pair, qm_elig_c_single, qm_elig_c_trajuneval): each logical column is TRUE where the row was eligible for (the denominator of) that step. Write-only — never affects any exclusion. Child rows only (NA on adult). For eligibility-normalized quality measures; usually paired with exclude_detail = TRUE. See vignette("output") §5c for the per-column definitions.
debug FALSE Output assembly Retain intermediate CSD z-score columns (sd.orig, sd.corr, tbc.sd, ctbc.sd) plus ±5%-wt / ±1 cm plus/minus perturbation z-scores (tbc.p_plus, tbc.p_minus, ctbc.p_plus, ctbc.p_minus); z-scores are child rows only (NA on adult). Also adds gc_internal_sex — gc’s interpreted integer sex (0/1/NA, all rows); the primary sex column carries the user’s verbatim submission.
exclude_detail FALSE Output assembly Add the step-level Detailed exclusion code in an exclude_detailed column (the default exclude column always carries the consolidated Summary code). See vignette("exclusion-codes") for the two levels and crosswalk.
mean_ht returned when the data has adult rows Output assembly Include a mean_ht column (TRUE always returns it; FALSE omits it): the adult algorithm’s calculated mean height (cm) (Adult Step 11H). The mean_ht column can be used by researchers who want a consistent height for evaluation of body mass index. Computed only from the subject’s finally-included heights and populated on every adult height row (an excluded or missing height row takes the value of the included height nearest in age); NA for child rows, adult weight rows, and all height rows of a subject with no included height. The value is always computed; this switch controls only whether it is returned. Auto-set TRUE by full_detail = TRUE.
full_detail FALSE Output assembly Convenience switch: enables exclude_detail + cf_detail + corr_detail + recenter_detail + debug + tri_exclude + display_gc_id + internal_detail + mean_ht together. Does not enable qm_detail (request it explicitly).
unit_error_range TRUE (default ON) Output assembly Add informational unit_error_range logical column. TRUE when a value’s magnitude is consistent with a metric/imperial unit-conversion error AND it is outside the plausible z = −3 to +3 band. Never affects exclude; not in exclude.levels. Child zn3/zp3 from child_z3_reference.csv.gz; adult from the embedded NHANES CSD reference. Also drives a soft warning when > 20% of a parameter group’s cleaned values are flagged (whole column may be in the wrong unit). Set FALSE to omit the column (and the warning).
display_gc_id FALSE Output assembly Add a gc_internal_id column to the output containing the id growthcleanr actually used internally: equals the user’s id when it was valid (no regen), or the auto-generated 1:N (in input row order) when id was absent / NA / non-unique and gc had to regenerate. Lets callers recover a reliable per-row key when their input id had problems (output id always preserves whatever the user supplied). Auto-set TRUE by full_detail = TRUE. Not needed for semi-wide/wide input returned as long output, where gc_internal_id is always returned.
quietly FALSE All steps Progress level. Default FALSE prints the minimal view (a “cleaning in progress” header, an X/Y batch/checkpoint counter, and the end cleaning summary); TRUE turns off the progress lines and the summary (warnings, and the one-time note for vector-style calls, still appear). For the detailed per-step view use verbose. See vignette("wrapper") → Progress output.
verbose FALSE All steps When TRUE, prints the detailed view: the milestone lines (preprocessing, per-batch cleaning-child / cleaning-adult) plus granular per-step diagnostics (CF/EWMA/SDE/Evil-twins pre-filter + iteration counts, adult step headers). Implies quietly = FALSE. Threaded into cleanchild() / cleanadult(). Development/debugging only.

1B. Child algorithm (passed through cleangrowth() into cleanchild())

Argument Default Used in Role
piv.z.wt.high 22 Child Step 7 Upper unrecentered CSD z cutoff for WEIGHTKG (all ages). Weight has no standardized low cutoff — the low-WT z asymptotes near -10 with a positive weight, so the absolute floors v<0.2/v<1 kg do that job.
piv.z.ht.low.young -25 Child Step 7 Lower unrecentered CSD z cutoff for HEIGHTCM at ageyears < 1
piv.z.ht.low.old -15 Child Step 7 Lower unrecentered CSD z cutoff for HEIGHTCM at ageyears >= 1
piv.z.ht.high 8 Child Step 7 Upper unrecentered CSD z cutoff for HEIGHTCM (all ages)
piv.z.hc.low -15 Child Step 7 Lower unrecentered CSD z cutoff for HEADCM (all ages)
piv.z.hc.high 15 Child Step 7 Upper unrecentered CSD z cutoff for HEADCM (all ages)
cf_rescue "standard" Child Step 6 CF rescue mode: "standard" (deltaz/nextz rule), "none" (all CFs excluded), "all" (all rescued). TRUE/FALSE stop with a pointer to the 2.x equivalent; other values are resolved by match.arg().
cf_detail FALSE Child Step 6; output If TRUE, add diagnostic columns cf_status, cf_deltaz, cf_nextz, imperial, cf_dage_orig, and cf_dage_next to output. cf_status adds "CF-E" (same-day-extraneous CF) alongside Orig/CF-R/CF-NR/Not-CF/Adult; in cf_rescue = "all", same-day CFs are labelled CF-R instead, with cf_deltaz and cf_dage_orig NA. cf_nextz is the signed change in sd.orig from each CF row to the next non-CF Included value at the time of Step 6 (temp SDEs skipped). The last three are design aids for CF-logic development: imperial (whole/half imperial-unit flag), cf_dage_orig (originator→CF day gap), cf_dage_next (CF→next-Included day gap).
ewma_window 15 Child Steps 11, 13, 15/16, 17; Adult Steps 9Wb, 11Wb Max observations on each side that contribute to EWMA weighting. Single parameter in cleangrowth() affecting both child and adult.
error.load.mincount 2 Child Step 21 Minimum “real” errors (not SDE / CF / Missing / Not-Cleaned) before error-load is evaluated
error.load.threshold 0.5 Child Step 21 Error ratio above which all remaining Include rows for the subject-param are excluded. Strict >.
length.adjust FALSE Preprocessing (before z-scores) If TRUE, reconciles entered linear measurements with what the reference at that age expects, in both directions (±0.7 cm at the 2-year boundary, day 730; pediatric-only; long input only). Full behavior is the SSOT in vignette("wrapper"), section “Length vs. height handling”. Arithmetic in .gc_to_metric() (reshape_adapters.R); called from child_clean.R → cleangrowth() inside the outer batch loop.

1C. Adult algorithm (wrapper-exposed)

These adult arguments are exposed directly through cleangrowth(); the individual permissiveness settings (Section 1D) are set by the preset and, if needed, overridden through adult_overrides.

Argument Default Used in Role
adult_permissiveness "looser" cleanadult preset resolver Preset level: "loosest", "looser", "tighter", "tightest" (case and surrounding spaces are ignored). Sets defaults for all adult settings.
adult_scale_max_lbs Inf Adult Step 4W Physical scale upper limit in pounds. Weights within ±0.1 kg of the cap are excluded if they are more than 50 kg different from their expected value, or if all of the subject’s weights (at least two) are the same value at the cap.
ewma_window 15 Adult Steps 9Wb, 11Wb See Section 1B — shared parameter with child; single value in cleangrowth() affects both algorithms.
adult_overrides NULL cleanadult preset resolver Optional named list overriding individual Section-1D settings, e.g. list(overall_ht_min = 120, allow_ht_gain = FALSE). Each named value replaces the preset value for that setting; unnamed or unrecognized names are an error. Adult rows only.

1D. Adult permissiveness presets (set by adult_permissiveness)

Cleaning is always imperfect, and there is always a tradeoff between over- and under-excluding measurements. Depending on the study population, research question, and analytic method, users may prioritize sensitivity or specificity. There are multiple settings in the adult algorithm that can be changed to adjust cleaning performance. The default values for these settings can be adjusted together using the adult_permissiveness argument or can be adjusted individually.

There are four permissiveness levels, set with the adult_permissiveness argument: loosest, looser, tighter, and tightest. The loosest setting will generally lead to the fewest exclusions, and tightest to the most exclusions. The looser setting is the default and is most similar to v2.2.3 (although not exactly the same). Descriptions and example use cases for the permissiveness options are below, followed by a table with the specific preset values and information regarding how to adjust settings individually. More detailed documentation of these settings is in vignette("adult-algorithm") (“Permissiveness Framework” and the step sections named in the Role column of the table below). Child-algorithm arguments are in Section 1B.

Permissiveness setting intended use and description

  • loosest: Intended for studies of patients who may have extreme size changes, and for which the priority is to retain all plausible values. Allows extreme weight changes (bariatric surgery, rapid fluid status change), significant height measurement error, height gain in young adults, and height loss.

  • looser (default): Intended for studies of a broad population of patients (who may include patients taking GLP-1 medication or having had bariatric surgery) but for which the user accepts exclusion of occasional plausible measurements for patients with extreme size or extreme size changes in order to exclude more values that likely represent error. Retains most plausible values. Slightly less extreme weights allowed. Height gain allowed; height loss beyond the 3-inch band is not.

  • tighter: Intended for studies that may include patients with atypical size (e.g., class 3 obesity) or relatively significant change in size, but for which retention of true extreme values or very unusual patterns is a lower priority than excluding most implausible measurements. May result in exclusion of some plausible values likely reflecting illness with large effect on body size. Less permissive height limits. Height gain allowed; height loss beyond the 2-inch band is not. Repeated values treated as less informative (see “Repeated Value (RV) Handling” in vignette("adult-algorithm")).

  • tightest: Intended for studies of relatively healthy populations and central tendencies. Excludes extreme measurements even if plausible given a patient’s other measurements. Tightest weight and height limits. No height gain or loss allowance. Repeated values treated as less informative (see “Repeated Value (RV) Handling” in vignette("adult-algorithm")). The allofus15 weight-allowance formula used at the tightest level was adapted from the algorithm developed by Guide et al. (2024) for the All of Us Research Program (full citation under “Permissiveness Framework” in vignette("adult-algorithm")).

ht_band (inches) 3 3 2 2 Height band tolerance (Adult Step 10H). Converted to cm via × 2.54 + 0.12.
allow_ht_loss TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE Whether height loss over time is allowed (Adult Step 10H)
allow_ht_gain TRUE TRUE TRUE FALSE Whether height gain over time is allowed (Adult Step 10H)
repval_handling independent independent linked linked Repeated-value handling mode (Adult Steps 2W, 9Wb, 11Wb)

To change one or a few without switching preset, pass them in the adult_overrides named list to cleangrowth() — e.g. cleangrowth(df, adult_permissiveness = "tighter", adult_overrides = list(overall_ht_min = 120)). The names must match the setting names in the table above; an unrecognized name is an error. (The value replaces the preset value for adult rows; it has no effect on child rows.)

1E. Removed arguments

include.carryforward and weight_cap are not valid cleangrowth() arguments. Use cf_rescue in place of include.carryforward, and adult_scale_max_lbs in place of weight_cap. For the full list of arguments removed since growthcleanr 2.2.3, see “Removed and renamed arguments” in vignette("experienced-start-here").
